description:
Bycatch from the fz-kdt.111 refutation (2026-09-01), all verified
IDENTICAL at base 24b228068 and head -- pre-existing, not introduced.
Probe programs parked at the session scratchpad k111/probes/.

(1) Enum.map over a LIST OF CLOSURES: interp dies 'backend executable 22
function 122 entry 2 tail failed: compiler2_unreachable_control'; JIT
prints the correct answer. Three-path-parity break, same family as
fz-kdt.111, different site (a tail, not a construction).

(2) A closure stored as a MAP VALUE (%{:p => fn(x) -> ... end}): JIT and
AOT abort (exit 134, non-unwinding panic in _fz_ref_load_int); head
interp now runs it CORRECTLY ([], true) -- fz-kdt.111 turned a
both-paths-red case into interp-green/JIT-abort, exposing the native bug.

(3) Two closures joined through an `if`, then passed to Enum.drop_while:
error[artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan] native lowering failure on both
run and build. Possibly fz-kdt.107/108 family (joined callable at a
dispatch surface) -- check there before fixing standalone.

Triage each separately when picked up; they share a smell, not a proven
root.
title: Three pre-existing parity/lowering bugs found by fz-kdt.111 refuter probes (closure-in-map JIT abort; Enum.map closure-list interp unreachable_control; if-joined closures incomplete-semantic-plan)
